target.name: Atomic Industries
target.founder: Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, Lou Young Jr

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, and Lou Young Jr., having raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company (277810.KQ), including peers at seed and Series B stages such as Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, applied to the $25M raised proxy, yielding $50M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector comparables—three at Series B and one at seed—produces a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The dispersion reflects stage variance within the peer set: Walden Robotics at seed ($1.1B) anchors the lower end, while Generalist AI at Series B ($2.0B) anchors the upper end.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range of $42M to $2.0B (median: $875M). The stage-progression result ($50M) reflects mechanical progression alone, while peer-median ($1.7B) reflects market-tested valuations in the target sector. Key uncertainties driving the range include stage comparability across the peer set and company-specific execution risk relative to named comparables. A defensible valuation likely falls between $100M–$400M, discounting the full peer-median for stage discount.
